item.text: The app uses the Next.js App Router and server-rendered product pages. I’m adding a small client navigation layer so the browser can capture the old and new routes during navigation, while matching each product’s grid and detail image by a shared transition name. The existing colored image blocks are the gallery’s image placeholders, so I’ll use those as the shared elements.

The shared image names and route links are in place. I’m finishing the motion styles now: product pages slide according to navigation direction, image groups morph between sizes, and detail content eases in after its Suspense fallback. The reduced motion setting disables both the browser transition and the CSS animation effects.

item.text:
Added native shared element transitions for product image placeholders, using matching names between each grid thumbnail and detail hero. Grid links slide forward to product pages, and the back link slides in the opposite direction. Detail content fades in after its Suspense skeleton.

The navigation layer checks `prefers-reduced-motion` and skips the browser transition when reduced motion is enabled; CSS also disables animations for that preference. Browsers without the View Transitions API fall back to normal navigation.

I ran `git diff --check`; it passed. I didn’t run the app or tests.

The existing changes to `package.json` and `package-lock.json` were already present before this work.
